EV scooter subscriptions in Bengaluru

Yulu and Bounce are the two largest electric scooter subscription operators in Bengaluru, and both have expanded their fleets steadily since 2022. Monthly plans start at Rs. 1,299 for a basic scooter with a standard battery, while premium plans with a swappable battery and insurance reach Rs. 2,499 per month. Both operators require a refundable deposit that typically ranges from Rs. 2,000 to Rs. 5,000 depending on the plan and the rider profile. Delivery partners account for a large share of long term subscriptions, because the plans include maintenance and battery swaps at no extra charge, which reduces downtime for people who depend on their vehicle for income.

Regulation in Karnataka treats shared electric two wheelers as transport vehicles, so operators need a licence from the state transport department and must register every scooter as a rental vehicle. The state electric vehicle policy offers a road tax exemption and capital subsidies for fleet operators who commit to charging infrastructure within city limits. Operators must also maintain third party insurance for each vehicle and report accidents to the authorities within forty eight hours. Compliance costs are modest for small fleets, but they rise quickly when operators scale beyond a few thousand vehicles across several zones of the city.

Unit economics depend heavily on utilisation and on battery swap logistics. Industry estimates put a healthy utilisation rate at four to six rides per scooter per day for pay per ride services, and above eighty percent of days rented for subscription fleets. A typical scooter costs between Rs. 90,000 and Rs. 1,10,000 to purchase, and payback periods of fourteen to twenty months are reported when utilisation stays stable. Theft, battery degradation and municipal parking rules remain the main sources of unplanned cost, and operators mitigate them with geofencing, telematics and partnerships with local garages that handle repairs quickly.

Analysts expect demand to keep growing through 2027 as fuel prices stay high and more employers offer commuting allowances for electric vehicles. However, competition from manufacturers who now sell directly on low interest financing could compress margins for subscription operators, especially in the premium segment where riders compare monthly costs against the total cost of ownership of a vehicle they could buy outright.
